docs.title: ADR-025: Federation vs Fleet DB — Decision Rule for Multi-Install Topology
docs.text:
Status: Proposed

Date: 2026-06-15

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
crackz now persists everything in a single, user-provided, single-tenant Postgres per install (ADR-023): one engine per process from CRACKZ_DATABASE_URL, many projects scoped by the project_id FK, no tenant_id, no row-level security. The sibling app survey_tool runs its own Postgres + pgvector + PostGIS on a CPU-only NAS (its ADR-004 capture_embeddings).

As crackz moves from single-site pilots to multi-install deployments (ADR-022) and builds out a complete RAG (#665, #627), a recurring question arises: do we need a shared "fleet" database — one Postgres holding many customers' operational data and vectors — or do we stay federated (one DB per app/install)? This ADR records the default, the explicit triggers that would justify crossing over, and the cost of crossing, so the decision is a deliberate one rather than an accidental drift.

This ADR does not introduce a fleet DB. It records the rule for when one would.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Stay federated. One user-provided, single-tenant Postgres per app/install remains the default and the only operational store, per ADR-023. The only sanctioned central store is the thin, opt-in telemetry backbone (ADR-022) — heartbeats and aggregate counters, no images, no PII — which is an analytics store, not an operational or embedding store.

Apps are coupled by versioned HTTP service contracts, never a shared DB or a cross-DB join. crackz ↔ survey_tool integration (#643) is federation-by-contract: crackz exposes inference over HTTP (POST /detect); survey_tool calls it and persists its own ImageFinding rows and its own embeddings in its own Postgres. Two independent pgvector stores, each with its own embedding_version lineage, joined only by a service call.

Decision rule — adopt a shared/multi-tenant fleet DB only when one of these triggers fires (and record the crossing in a follow-up ADR):

  1. Cross-customer / cross-install similarity search becomes a product requirement ("similar defects across all harbors", not within one install). Federated per-install vector stores cannot answer this without centralizing vectors.
  2. Centralized model-improvement corpus — pooling crops / embeddings / labels from many installs into one training/eval corpus. Try satisfying this via export pipelines into the telemetry/analytics backend first; that often does not require a shared operational DB.
  3. SaaS control plane (#17) is greenlit — the only roadmap item that plans real multi-tenancy (~24 weeks out per ADR-022), and the natural home for tenant_id + RLS + auth.
  4. Customer multi-site dashboard (#6) needs live operational cross-site joins beyond the aggregated heartbeats ADR-022 already provides. Try the telemetry backbone first.
  5. Operational scale where administering per-install Postgres (backups, upgrades, pgvector index maintenance across dozens of installs) costs more than running one managed multi-tenant cluster.

Schema-readiness: YAGNI on tenancy. Do not add tenant_id now. To be correct it must propagate into every FK scope, index, unique constraint, and repository query; a nullable-but-ignored column is a latent bug magnet (queries that forget to filter it leak rows across tenants). When multi-tenancy actually lands (#17), do it as a deliberate RLS migration. A nullable install_id may be added only at the telemetry seam, and only when ADR-022's backend needs to correlate operational rows with heartbeats — it is telemetry metadata, not a tenancy axis.

Swappable-seam invariant. All vector access funnels through core/src/crackz/db/repositories/ (e.g. embeddings.py, and the planned doc_embeddings.py); callers depend on the repository / retrieval seam, never on pgvector SQL directly. This keeps a future vector-tier change (e.g. Qdrant; see ADR-026) a backend swap rather than a rewrite, and is a maintained invariant, not an accident.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Benefit: preserves FK integrity within each app (cascade-delete of detections cleans up embeddings), the offline-first / on-prem posture customers expect, and independent deployability/versioning per app. No auth, RLS, network exposure, or data-residency story is forced before it is needed.
  • Benefit: the cost of multi-tenancy is sized and gated, so it is paid once, deliberately, at the SaaS/cross-install boundary — not accreted column-by-column.
  • Trade-off: cross-install questions ("across all harbors") are not answerable today without centralizing vectors. Accepted: no current product requirement needs it, and triggers 1–2 above name the moment to revisit.
  • Trade-off: per-install Postgres administration scales linearly with install count. Mitigated by ADR-022 telemetry visibility and documented ops; trigger 5 names the crossover.
  • Follow-up: when a trigger fires, write the crossing ADR sizing tenant_id on every table + index + unique constraint, RLS + a tenant-context session layer, authn/authz (reuse ADR-022 per-install API-key issuance), network + TLS + data-residency, and embedding-version coordination across tenants (a shared HNSW index forces globally coordinated model_name / embedding_version / dim; the defect_embeddings UNIQUE key and fixed vector(768) column all gain a tenant dimension).

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Shared multi-tenant operational/embedding DB now: enables cross-install analytics and cross-customer similarity immediately. Rejected — no current product requirement needs it; it forces auth, tenant_id, RLS, network exposure, and a data-residency story onto an on-prem product (consistent with ADR-023's rejection).
  • Federated + a half-wired tenant_id seam now ("cheap future-proofing"): rejected — a nullable column that is not enforced in every query is a correctness hazard; the install_id-at-telemetry-seam option captures the only cheap, safe part.
  • A shared DB just for the model-improvement corpus: rejected as the default — prefer export pipelines into the ADR-022 analytics backend, which avoids making the operational store shared. Revisit under trigger 2 if exports prove insufficient.

docs.title: ADR-026: Text/Doc RAG over pgvector + Unified Retrieval Seam
docs.text:
Status: Proposed

Date: 2026-06-15

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
crackz has two disjoint, partial retrieval surfaces:

  • Image similarity (semantic, server-side): defect_embeddings.embedding vector(768) (DINOv2-base, L2-normalized), HNSW cosine <=> filtered by project_id + model_name + embedding_version with hnsw.iterative_scan (core/src/crackz/db/repositories/embeddings.py).
  • Doc/chat search (keyword, not semantic, GUI-local): ADR-021 SQLite FTS5 over docs/*.md, chunked at ##, top-3 chunks injected into the Claude system prompt (gui/src/crackz_gui/services/ai_chat.py, gui/src/crackz_gui/data/{doc_chunker,chat_history_db}.py).

There are no text embeddings anywhere yet, and FTS5 misses semantic synonyms (ADR-021 names this: "convergence" vs "loss not improving"). #665 asks whether to upgrade chat doc-search from keyword to semantic RAG now that pgvector exists in-tree (ADR-023). The complication is operational: core's pgvector needs a reachable Postgres and a text embedder, but the chat app is an offline-first desktop Qt app, and the import-linter forbids the GUI from importing crackz.cli and crackz.ai.* from importing crackz.cli. A decision is needed to pick the doc-RAG storage, embedder, and where it runs without breaking offline-first.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Build text/doc RAG on the existing pgvector substrate, behind a swappable retrieval seam, served as a core/server capability, with a hybrid desktop story that preserves offline-first.

Storage — a separate doc_embeddings table (new Alembic migration 0004). Do not reuse defect_embeddings: it is image-specific (DINOv2-fixed dim; FKs to detection_result_id/detection_run_id; GPS/bbox/mask semantics). doc_embeddings mirrors the patterns (idempotent upsert, HNSW cosine, version columns), not the columns: - id, doc_path, header, chunk_index, chunk_text, model_name, embedding_version, dim, embedding vector(768), created_at; optional nullable project_id only if docs ever become project-scoped (default: global docs → none). - UNIQUE (doc_path, chunk_index, model_name, embedding_version) for idempotent re-index (mirrors the ON CONFLICT pattern in insert_embeddings). - HNSW vector_cosine_ops with the same hnsw.iterative_scan / ef_search tuning as search() in embeddings.py.

Embedder — local Ollama (e.g. nomic-embed-text, 768-dim), reusing the local Ollama endpoint the GUI already talks to. This keeps doc-RAG offline-capable, adds no heavy in-app dependency, and fixes doc_embedding_dim = 768 (the same width as DINOv2 by coincidence — doc_embeddings remains a separate table because model and provenance differ). New settings: doc_embedding_model_name, doc_embedding_dim, doc_embedding_version in crackz_settings.py.

Seam — a RetrievalBackend protocol shared by image and doc search, with a common SearchHit DTO. core/src/crackz/db/repositories/doc_embeddings.py mirrors embeddings.py (insert_doc_embeddings, search, rows_needing_embedding). A no-Typer doc-RAG function lives in embedding/service.py style.

Serving — one FastAPI app, one GPU host, sharing inference and retrieval: POST /detect (wraps DetectionRunner, #643), POST /embed + POST /search (image), POST /rag (docs). All endpoints emit versioned JSON carrying model_version / embedding_version so federated callers pin compatibility.

Desktop — hybrid (server-semantic + FTS5 offline). ai_chat.py's _get_context() selects a backend by availability: when a crackz retrieval service / Postgres is reachable, use pgvector doc-RAG (/rag); otherwise fall back to FTS5 (ADR-021), optionally with a small local Ollama rerank of FTS5 candidates. The GUI calls a core retrieval function or the HTTP service — never crackz.cli, never crackz.db directly — so import-linter contracts hold and the offline guarantee is preserved.

Qdrant — contingency only. Stay on pgvector. Trip to Qdrant only on a measured trigger (recall/latency target unmet after ef_search/iterative_scan tuning; vector count outgrows one Postgres node; or a dedicated cross-app vector tier — which also implies an ADR-025 crossing). Because all vector access funnels through the repository / RetrievalBackend seam, adding Qdrant is a new backend implementing the same interface, selected by config, with no change to service.py, the endpoints, or callers.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Benefit: semantic doc/chat retrieval that beats FTS5 on synonyms, reusing the pgvector infra and versioning patterns already in-tree (no second vector DB, no ChromaDB — the originally-descoped #311–#315 stack).
  • Benefit: offline-first is preserved — the desktop degrades cleanly to FTS5 with no Postgres dependency; the heavy path is a server capability.
  • Benefit: one FastAPI app serves both survey_tool inference (#643) and retrieval; the embedder loads once on the GPU host.
  • Trade-off: semantic doc-RAG requires a reachable service/Postgres; full quality is not available purely offline. Accepted via the hybrid fallback.
  • Trade-off: a new table, migration, settings, and a text embedder to maintain, plus a re-index story for docs (parallels defect_embeddings embedding versioning).
  • Follow-up: build the FastAPI app (#643 Phase 1) and /rag (Phase 2); wire the GUI hybrid seam (Phase 3); revisit Qdrant only under a measured trigger (Phase 4).

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Keep FTS5 only (ADR-021 status quo): cheapest, fully offline, but misses semantic synonyms. Rejected as the end state, kept as the offline fallback.
  • ChromaDB + sentence-transformers (the original #311–#315 RAG): +100MB deps, cold-start indexing, a Qt background thread. Rejected — disproportionate and redundant now that pgvector is the maintained substrate (this is why #311–#315 were descoped).
  • Reuse defect_embeddings for text: rejected — different dim, model, and provenance; image FKs and GPS/bbox/mask semantics do not apply to doc chunks; mixing fidelities in one HNSW index degrades ranking.
  • Hosted text-embedding API (OpenAI/Voyage): highest quality, smallest local footprint, but needs network + an API key and breaks offline-first. Rejected for the default; the seam leaves it available if a server-only deployment wants it.
  • Qdrant now: rejected — pgvector suffices at current scale; Qdrant is gated behind the swappable seam (ADR-025 invariant) for when a measured limit is hit.

docs.title: ADR-027: GPS-Filtered Defect Similarity Ranking (filter-then-blend, PostGIS-only)
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Date: 2026-06-15

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Phase 1 (#627/#653, ADR-023) gave crackz pure-visual defect similarity: defect_embeddings.embedding vector(768) (DINOv2-base, L2-normalized), HNSW cosine <=> filtered by project_id + model_name + embedding_version with hnsw.iterative_scan (core/src/crackz/db/repositories/embeddings.py::search).

Phase 2 (#661) asks for geospatially-aware retrieval: "find visually similar defects within N metres of this one." Visual search and GPS filtering already exist independently — embeddings.py::search (visual) and geo.py::find_detections_near (ST_DWithin radius, operating on detection_results, not joined to embeddings) — but they have never been combined. The issue spec proposes a blended score final_score = visual_similarity + gps_weight·proximity (+ temporal + class), with temporal/class deferred to Phase 3 (#662).

Two design forces need a recorded decision because they are easy to get wrong and expensive to reverse:

  1. Where filtering happens relative to the ANN cut. Filtering by radius in Python after a top_k ANN LIMIT silently drops neighbors that are visually-close-but-just-inside-radius, because the LIMIT already truncated them — a recall bug that is invisible in small test sets.
  2. What happens when PostGIS is absent. foto-dator runs PostGIS per ADR-023, but the GUI must never crash a view when the DB or PostGIS is unavailable — and, critically, foto-dator is underwater, so a detection with no GPS is a normal mode, not an edge case. The "no geospatial filtering available" path must be first-class.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Filter to the radius inside SQL, then order by the blended score — a new search_with_gps() in the repository layer (embeddings.py), exposed through the existing CLI-free embedding/service.py seam and called by both the CLI and the GUI.

  • Filter-then-blend in SQL. When radius_m is set, an ST_DWithin predicate on the embedding row's geometry prunes candidates with/inside the ANN scan (the hnsw.iterative_scan guard from search() is carried over), and the surviving rows are ordered by final_score computed in SQL. This preserves recall: the radius prunes before the LIMIT truncates, not after.
  • Score formula (Phase 2 = visual + GPS only).
  • visual_similarity = 1 − cosine_distance / 2 (range [0, 1], L2-normalized embeddings).
  • proximity = 1 − distance_m / radius_m (linear falloff: 1 at the query point, 0 at the radius edge).
  • final_score = visual_similarity + gps_weight · proximity, computed in SQL and ordered descending, with a (detection_result_id, crop_index) tiebreaker for deterministic ranking.
  • Weights are configurable in CrackzSettings: embedding_gps_weight (default 0.15); embedding_temporal_weight / embedding_class_weight ship inert (0.0) so Phase 3 can activate them with no schema or signature change. All weights are Field(ge=0.0) (negative weights rejected).
  • NULL-GPS rows are excluded under a radius. Rows with NULL gps_* / NULL geom cannot be placed, so ST_DWithin naturally excludes them. Pure-visual search (radius_m is None) still includes them. Documented in the service docstring.
  • PostGIS-only — no Haversine fallback. Implement the ST_DWithin path only. When PostGIS is unavailable and a radius was requested, search_with_gps raises PostGISUnavailableError; the service catches it and degrades to pure-visual search, returning a SearchResult(hits, gps_applied=False, fallback_reason="no_postgis") wrapper rather than silently changing its return shape. When the query point itself has no GPS, the service degrades the same way with fallback_reason="no_gps".
  • The degradation is visible, not silent. SearchResult.gps_applied / .fallback_reason (∈ {None, "no_postgis", "no_gps"}) is the seam contract. The CLI prints a stderr note; the GUI's defect-comparison view shows a first-class "GPS filtering unavailable" banner. Absent-GPS is a normal mode (foto-dator is underwater), so this UX is required, not a corner case.

radius_m <= 0 short-circuits to [] before the PostGIS check, so an explicit empty radius never trips the unavailable path.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Benefit: "visually similar cracks within 50 m" works as one ranked query, with recall preserved because the radius prunes inside the ANN scan.
  • Benefit: degradation is observable — callers branch on gps_applied / fallback_reason instead of guessing from a changed return type; the GUI shows why GPS filtering did not run.
  • Benefit: Phase 3 (temporal/class) drops in by flipping the inert weights — no migration, no signature change.
  • Trade-off: GPS ranking requires PostGIS; there is no offline/SQLite geospatial path. Accepted (ADR-023 makes Postgres+PostGIS the substrate) and made safe by the pure-visual degradation.
  • Trade-off: GpsSearchHit subclasses SearchHit and adds distance_m / final_score; consumers must read those with getattr(..., None) since they are present only when gps_applied is True.
  • Follow-up: Phase 3 (#662) activates temporal/class weights; the pre-existing pure-visual search() ORDER BY still lacks the tiebreaker added here (out of scope; flag if touched).

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Filter in Python after the ANN top_k cut: simplest, but drops in-radius-but-just-past-LIMIT neighbors → silent recall loss. Rejected.
  • Haversine fallback when PostGIS is absent (mirroring geo.py::find_detections_near): keeps GPS ranking working without PostGIS, but duplicates distance math, can't push the predicate into the HNSW scan, and adds a second code path to keep correct. Rejected for Phase 2 — ADR-023 guarantees PostGIS on foto-dator; pure-visual degradation covers the gap.
  • Raise/return-None on PostGIS-absent instead of a wrapper: forces every caller into try/except and hides the "we fell back" signal. Rejected in favor of the explicit SearchResult wrapper (the seam contract).
  • Single combined search(..., radius_m=None) instead of a new search_with_gps(): overloads one function with two SQL shapes and risks regressing the Phase-1 pure-visual path. Rejected — a separate function keeps the visual path untouched.

docs.title: ADR-028: Defect Track Temporal Progression (B-minimal)
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Date: 2026-06-15

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Phase 1 (#627/#653, ADR-023) gave crackz pgvector-backed visual similarity search. Phase 2 (#661, ADR-027) added GPS-filtered ranking via a filter-then-blend SQL query (search_with_gps) and shipped the embedding_temporal_weight config key inert at 0.0 for Phase 3 to activate.

Phase 3 (#662) takes the first slice: temporal progression — letting an inspector see how one physical defect evolved across separate inspection runs. The data model has no concept of defect identity across inspections: every detection_results row is independent, and the only signals for "this June crack is the same crack as in March" are visual similarity (DINOv2 cosine distance), GPS proximity (geom/gps_latitude/gps_longitude), and inspection time (detection_runs.run_at). Each signal has gaps:

  • Visual similarity false-matches look-alike cracks, and a worsening defect drifts visually — the case we most care about is the one matching defeats.
  • GPS is frequently NULL because foto-dator is underwater — a normal mode, not an edge case (established in ADR-027).
  • Inspection time orders runs but says nothing about identity.

A stored, correctable representation of defect tracks is also the substrate the future anomaly-evolution slice will need, so deferring to query-only history would require rebuilding it later.

Three design options were considered:

  • Option A (implicit query): history = on-demand similarity search grouped by run_at, nothing persisted.
  • Option B-minimal (chosen): a stored defect_tracks identity table, auto- proposed links the inspector can confirm/reject, and a dedicated ProgressionView. Full curation UI deferred.
  • Full Option B: B-minimal + complete split/merge/reassign curation UI in the same slice.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: B-minimal: a thin stored defect_tracks identity table, auto-proposed links (visual similarity + optional GPS tiebreak) via an idempotent track link command, and a ProgressionView for display.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
defect_tracks is deliberately thin — pure identity:

column type notes id BigInteger PK, Identity project_id BigInteger FK → projects.id ON DELETE CASCADE indexed created_at TIMESTAMPTZ server_default=now()

Severity, category, confidence, GPS, and time all live on detection_results/detection_runs and are derived by joining. Duplicating them on the track would cause drift.

Track membership and link metadata are added to detection_results (one detection belongs to at most one track):

column type notes track_id BigInteger FK → defect_tracks.id ON DELETE SET NULL, nullable NULL = unlinked track_link_status Text, nullable proposed / confirmed / rejected track_link_cosine Double, nullable raw pgvector <=> cosine distance [0,2] that justified the proposal track_link_distance_m Double, nullable GPS distance (m) at proposal time; NULL when GPS absent

track_link_cosine stores raw cosine distance (the pgvector <=> convention); the similarity used for threshold comparison is derived as 1 - distance/2, matching ADR-027.

docs.title: Migration 0004: run_at TEXT → TIMESTAMPTZ
docs.text:
detection_runs.run_at is the chronological sort key for the whole feature. Keeping it TEXT in a temporal feature is a liability. Every existing value is written as UTC ISO-8601 (datetime.now(UTC).isoformat() in detection_runner; mtime.isoformat() in app/projects), so the cast is safe:

ALTER TABLE detection_runs ALTER COLUMN run_at TYPE TIMESTAMPTZ USING run_at::timestamptz;

Blast radius (updated together in this migration): db/models.py (run_at Mapped[str] → Mapped[datetime]), db/records.py DTO fields, read sites in metrics_store.py, repositories/geo.py, repositories/detections.py, cli/geo_cli.py, sqlite_import.py, and integration test assertions comparing run_at to literal ISO strings.

docs.title: Settings (new, config/crackz_settings.py, embedding_* convention)
docs.text:
• embedding_track_sim_threshold: float = 0.85 — minimum cosine similarity to propose a link. Both are Field(ge=0.0).
  • embedding_track_radius_m: float = 50.0 — GPS inclusion radius (metres) for the tiebreak. Matches the example radius used throughout the #661 design.

docs.title: Matching rule (auto-linker, Python-only — no PostGIS dependency)
docs.text:
For each detection with an embedding (current model_name + embedding_version):

  1. Find the best candidate in other runs where visual_similarity ≥ embedding_track_sim_threshold (visual_similarity = 1 - cosine_distance / 2, the ADR-027 convention).
  2. When both sides have GPS, additionally require distance_m ≤ embedding_track_radius_m; rank candidates by proximity as a tiebreak. When either side lacks GPS (underwater), fall back to visual-only — the GPS clause is skipped, not failed.
  3. Transitive grouping (union-find): if A↔B and B↔C both match, A, B, C share one track, not three. Pairwise matches collapse into a single defect_tracks row.

The linker loads every project embedding for the current model/version once, then computes pairwise cosine similarity (dot product, L2-normalised vectors) and the GPS tiebreak (Haversine) entirely in Python with a union-find collapse. It does not call search_with_gps, does not use ST_DWithin, and has no PostGIS dependency. This is O(n²) in detections-per-project; acceptable for B-minimal. Blocking/ANN candidate generation is noted as a future optimisation.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text: propose_links (the repository function that drives track link) is idempotent: re-runs touch only proposed/unlinked rows and reuse the existing proposed track for a group (no duplicate defect_tracks rows are created). Confirmed links are never overwritten; rejected stays rejected unless explicitly reset.

docs.title: Layering
docs.text:
GUI/CLI → service (ai/embedding/service.py or ai/tracking/: link_tracks, history_for_detection, confirm, reject, TrackHistory value object) → repository (db/repositories/tracks.py: propose_links, confirm_link, reject_link, track_history) → DB.

Service and repository import neither Typer nor Qt, matching the Phase 2 seam discipline. The service is also the REST seam for the future #643 endpoint.

docs.title: Known limitation
docs.text: A worsening defect that drifts visually below embedding_track_sim_threshold will not be auto-linked, and B-minimal has no manual-add UI yet (split/merge/ reassign are deferred to the anomaly-evolution slice). This is a known limitation, documented openly here rather than hidden.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Benefit: Inspectors gain a durable, correctable record of defect identity across runs — confirmed links survive re-embedding and CLI re-runs.
  • Benefit: The linker is PostGIS-independent (pure Python + Haversine), so GPS tiebreak works on any Postgres deployment and has no degrade path to manage.
  • Benefit: ProgressionView + track history CLI surface the full inspection timeline including visual drift (cosine of each member vs the earliest member).
  • Benefit: The thin defect_tracks table is the stored substrate the anomaly-evolution slice will need; deferring it would require rebuilding it then.
  • Trade-off: O(n²) pairwise linking is acceptable for B-minimal project sizes but will need blocking or ANN candidate generation as projects grow.
  • Trade-off: A worsening defect that drifts below the similarity threshold is not auto-linked and cannot yet be corrected manually (no split/merge UI).
  • Trade-off: embedding_temporal_weight stays inert this slice; a history is a grouping by time, not a re-ranking. The weight stays at 0.0 until the dedicated ranking slice.
  • Follow-up: split/merge/reassign curation UI → anomaly-evolution slice.
  • Follow-up: embed-time auto-link hook (standalone track link ships first for link-correctness validation).
  • Follow-up: activating embedding_temporal_weight as a ranking term → separate Phase 3 slice.

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Option A (ephemeral query-only history): History = on-demand similarity search grouped by run_at, nothing persisted. Fastest to implement, but a "track" is ephemeral, cannot be corrected, cannot represent a worsening defect, and would need to be rebuilt as a stored entity for anomaly-evolution anyway. Rejected.
  • Full Option B (B-minimal + complete curation UI this slice): Adds split/merge/reassign UI in the same work unit. Too large for one plan; curation UI is deferred to the anomaly-evolution slice. Rejected for scope.
  • PostGIS-based linker (ST_DWithin in SQL): The Phase 2 search_with_gps approach uses ST_DWithin inside the HNSW scan for per-query ranking. All-pairs linking across a project is a different shape (grouping, not ranking), so pushing it into SQL gains little and adds a PostGIS degrade path to manage. Haversine in Python with union-find is simpler and equally correct at B-minimal scale. Rejected.

docs.title: Related

docs.title: ADR-029: Assisted Classification (Confirmed-Pool Suggestion)
docs.text:
Status: Accepted

Date: 2026-06-16

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Issue #662 (Embeddings Phase 3, under #627) has four acceptance criteria. The historical progression view shipped in PR #684 (ADR-028, merged 2026-06-15). Three remain: clustering, assisted classification, and anomaly evolution. This ADR covers the assisted-classification slice only.

Assisted classification: when a new defect is visually close to known verified defects, suggest a likely class, a severity estimate, and related cases — with the inspector always verifying and approving. The AI suggests only; it never writes a classification back.

The existing data model has no dedicated "verified" flag and no inspection-records table separate from detection_results. What #684 added is track_link_status ∈ {proposed, confirmed, rejected} on detection_results, representing an inspector's approval of a temporal link between runs. That is the only human-in-the-loop signal currently available.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Verified pool = detections with track_link_status = 'confirmed'. This reuses #684's human-in-the-loop signal with no new table and no migration.

docs.title: Search filter
docs.text: The existing search() in db/repositories/embeddings.py uses an HNSW index with hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order to avoid the filtered-recall problem when a tight metadata filter would otherwise starve results below top_k. A new optional confirmed_only: bool = False parameter restricts the scan to track_link_status = 'confirmed' via an EXISTS subquery against detection_results, keeping the driving scan on defect_embeddings — the same shape as search_with_gps — so the HNSW iterative-scan recall path is preserved. The query's own row is excluded post-search by detection_result_id in the service layer (tolerant of absence, following the existing search_by_detection pattern).

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
suggest_classification() in ai/embedding/service.py returns a ClassificationSuggestion with:

  • Suggested class (primary_category): cosine-similarity-weighted vote over confirmed neighbours, skipping NULL-category neighbours.
  • Single suggested severity (defect_severity or crack_severity): defect_severity and crack_severity are populated identically in the multiclass workflow; we vote once using each neighbour's defect_severity or crack_severity, mirroring the existing pdf_exporter.py fallback.
  • Related cases: the confirmed neighbour SearchHit list.
  • A "k of n agreed" support count per label (k = neighbours voting for the winning value; n = neighbours with a non-NULL value for that field).
  • A min-support floor (default 2): a label whose n < min_support is suppressed and reason="insufficient_support" is set, but related cases are still returned. A (1, 1) agreement built on a single sample is not surfaced as a suggestion.

docs.title: Suggest-only
docs.text: The service never writes a category or severity back. Applying a suggestion is the inspector's existing detection-edit action, out of scope here.

docs.title: Surface
docs.text:
• CLI: crackz classify suggest <detection_result_id> [--top-k 10] [--min-support 2] in a new cli/classify_cli.py, registered in cli/crackz_cli.py.
  • GUI: a read-only SuggestionView (BaseView subclass) wired into detection_gallery_widget.py, data loaded off the UI thread following the same worker pattern as ProgressionView.

docs.title: Honest limitation
docs.text:
track_link_status = 'confirmed' means an inspector approved a temporal link between runs — that the June detection and the March detection are the same physical defect. It does not mean the detection's class or severity was independently verified. The voted labels are the same segmentation model's primary_category / defect_severity that produced the query detection, and a confirmed row can even have primary_category = NULL.

This feature is precedent retrieval among human-vetted recurring defects, not a verified ground-truth label store. The value is "here are visually similar defects an inspector found worth tracking, and what the model called them" — surfaced for the inspector to judge, never auto-applied. This limitation must be communicated clearly wherever the feature is documented or surfaced.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• When a real verified-classification store lands (e.g. a dedicated inspection-records table as anticipated in #627), it supersedes the confirmed-pool proxy. The confirmed_only search filter and the similarity-weighted vote are reusable unchanged.
  • No new table, no migration. The SearchHit dataclass gains defect_severity and crack_severity fields (NULL on non-confirmed paths); GpsSearchHit inherits them and the GPS search path is unaffected.
  • Clustering and anomaly evolution — the other two #662 criteria — are separate future slices. This ADR and its PR do not close #662.

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Dedicated verified-classifications / inspection-records table (separate from detection IDs, per #627): this would be the proper future home for inspector-verified labels and would supersede the confirmed-pool proxy. Rejected for now as premature / YAGNI at this slice.
  • Python-side filtering after a broad top-N search (fetch top-N, filter confirmed in Python): the filtered-recall problem bites exactly when confirmed defects are rare (early adoption); a fixed top_k can return zero confirmed neighbours. Rejected.
  • Numeric confidence model: more complex and no more honest than a support count when the pool is small. The "k of n" indicator is simpler and transparent. Rejected.

docs.title: Database setup (Postgres + pgvector + PostGIS)
docs.text:
Crackz stores project history, detections, and vector embeddings in Postgres. Two extensions are required or recommended:

  • pgvector (required) — stores and queries DINOv2 embedding vectors.
  • PostGIS (recommended) — enables geo find-near spatial queries. Without it crackz falls back to a Python Haversine path automatically.

All three deployment paths below end at the same state:

  1. vector and postgis extensions enabled on the crackz database.
  2. CRACKZ_DATABASE_URL pointing at that database.
  3. crackz db init run to apply Alembic migrations.

docs.title: Minimum requirements
docs.text:
Component Minimum Postgres 16+ pgvector 0.8+ (required) PostGIS 3.4+ (recommended)

pgvector 0.8+ is required because similarity search enables HNSW iterative scan (hnsw.iterative_scan), which keeps the result set at full size when a project/model filter is applied; that setting does not exist on earlier pgvector.

CRACKZ_DATABASE_URL is the single configuration knob. Set it in the environment or in a .env file at the project root. The default value works out of the box with the Docker path below:

CRACKZ_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://crackz:crackz@localhost:5432/crackz

docs.title: Docker (dev / quickstart)
docs.text:
The fastest path. A compose file is provided that runs Postgres 16 with both extensions pre-installed.

# Start the database in the background
docker compose -f core/docker-compose.dev.yml up -d

# Apply migrations (no extra env needed — defaults match the compose file)
crackz db init

The compose file builds a small local image (core/Dockerfile.postgres) that layers PostGIS onto the official, multi-arch pgvector/pgvector:pg16 image, so a single container provides both vector and postgis. crackz db init runs the migrations, which CREATE EXTENSION for both.

To stop and remove the container (data is preserved in the named volume):

docker compose -f core/docker-compose.dev.yml down

To also drop the data volume:

docker compose -f core/docker-compose.dev.yml down -v

docs.title: Bare metal (on-prem, e.g. foto-dator)
docs.text: Install Postgres 16, the pgvector extension package, and PostGIS for your distro, then create the database and role.

docs.title: Debian / Ubuntu
docs.text:
# Add the PGDG repository if not already present
sudo apt-get install -y curl ca-certificates
sudo install -d /usr/share/postgresql-common/pgdg
curl -o /usr/share/postgresql-common/pgdg/apt.postgresql.org.asc \
     --fail https://www.postgresql.org/media/keys/ACCC4CF8.asc
# Follow https://wiki.postgresql.org/wiki/Apt for the full repo setup

sudo apt-get install -y postgresql-16 postgresql-16-pgvector postgis

docs.title: Create database and role
docs.text:
-- Run as a Postgres superuser (e.g. sudo -u postgres psql)
CREATE ROLE crackz WITH LOGIN PASSWORD 'crackz';
CREATE DATABASE crackz OWNER crackz;

\c crackz

-- CREATE EXTENSION requires superuser unless the extension is trusted.
-- Run these as superuser, not as the crackz role.
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS postgis;

-- Grant schema usage to the application role
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO crackz;

Privilege note: CREATE EXTENSION normally requires superuser. Some managed Postgres distributions lower this bar; on plain bare-metal installs run the extension commands as the postgres superuser, not as the crackz application role.

docs.title: Configure and run migrations
docs.text:
export CRACKZ_DATABASE_URL="postgresql+psycopg://crackz:crackz@localhost:5432/crackz"
crackz db init

If you are importing history from an older SQLite project database, point the importer at the project (it reads that project's artifacts/project.db):

crackz db migrate-sqlite --project path/to/project   # or --cfg path/to/project.yaml

docs.title: Hosted / managed (RDS, Cloud SQL, Supabase, Azure)
Extension availability
docs.text:
Provider pgvector PostGIS Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Yes (>=15.2) Yes Google Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL Yes Yes Supabase Yes (built-in) Yes (built-in) Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server Yes Yes Neon Yes Varies by plan

Check your provider's current docs — extension availability changes with product tiers and versions.

docs.title: Enable extensions
docs.text:
Most managed providers expose a UI toggle or a single SQL command:

-- Run once after creating the database
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS postgis;

Some providers (e.g. Supabase) enable pgvector automatically — skip the CREATE EXTENSION vector step if it is already present.

docs.title: Set the connection URI
docs.text:
Managed databases typically require TLS. Append ?sslmode=require (or sslmode=verify-full if you have a CA cert):

export CRACKZ_DATABASE_URL="postgresql+psycopg://crackz:<password>@<host>:5432/crackz?sslmode=require"

Then run migrations:

crackz db init

docs.title: PostGIS-absent fallback
docs.text: If PostGIS is unavailable on your provider or disabled by policy, crackz still runs normally. The geo find-near command degrades gracefully to a Python Haversine calculation — slower for large datasets but functionally equivalent. No configuration change is needed; crackz detects the missing extension at startup.

docs.title: Database unreachable
docs.text:
On startup, both the CLI and the Qt GUI probe the database connection. If the database cannot be reached:

  • CLI — logs a WARNING to the console.
  • GUI — logs the same warning and shows a notice in the status bar: ⚠ No database connection — start Postgres (see docs/ops/database.md).

The application keeps running in both cases, but features that require a live database (detection persistence, embeddings search, geo queries, the dashboard) will fail until the database is up.

Fix: start the database and apply migrations (see Docker quickstart):

docker compose -f core/docker-compose.dev.yml up -d
crackz db init

Or point CRACKZ_DATABASE_URL at a reachable database before launching.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
Command Description crackz db init Run Alembic migrations to create or update the schema. Safe to run repeatedly. crackz db migrate-sqlite Import legacy project.db (SQLite) history into Postgres.

Both commands are being added as part of the Postgres migration feature (issue #627). Run crackz db --help for up-to-date options.
